newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie falls 4.5 pct on TNT charge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie falls 4.5 pct on TNT charge.

text.p: Shares in investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd dropped forty cents or 4.5 percent to A$8.40 in early afternoon trade after Macquarie announced that one of its executive directors had been charged under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, brokers said.
"It's a real shock to the market, particularly given it's a fairly major charge against an executive director," said one stockbroker who asked not to be named.
"It's certainly a negative for the stock," he said.
The charge was connected to the investigation into trading in TNT Ltd options before the A$2 billion takeover bid by Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
Macquarie said the executive charged, Simon Hannes, intended to plead not guilty to the charges.
Hannes is a senior executive of the bank's corporate advisory division, but was not part of the team working on the TNT transaction, Macquarie said.
Hannes had been on extended leave from Macquarie from August 1, 1996, but was available for part time consultation, Macquarie said.
Macquarie was the adviser to TNT on the eventually successful takeover bid.
At 0500 GMT (4 p.m.), Macquarie shares were at A$8.45, down 30 cents on Friday's close, after touching A$8.90 in early trade, equal to its 12-month high.
They were at A$8.80 when it announced Hannes had been charged.
